quests.instruction: While reading aloud, Noor mispronounces a word and the class giggles. Her cheeks turn warm and she looks down at the page. What is she most likely feeling?
quests.hint: Think about the moment when many eyes notice a small slip.
quests.explanation: Embarrassed is the warm, self-conscious feeling when others notice a slip. It is a very common feeling, and it does not mean anything is wrong with us.
quests.funFact: Almost everyone has had an embarrassing moment, and many people laugh about it later.

quests.instruction: Tom finally swims a full length of the pool without stopping. He climbs out, grinning, and stands a little taller. Pick the best word for his feeling.
quests.hint: Think about what he worked for and what he just did.
quests.explanation: Proud is the warm, satisfied feeling about something we worked hard on. It is tied to our effort, not just to luck.
quests.funFact: Noticing your own progress can bring pride without comparing yourself to anyone else.

quests.instruction: It is Sunday afternoon. Everyone in the building is out, the street is quiet, and Mia drifts from room to room wishing someone would come and play. What is she feeling?
quests.hint: Notice what she is wishing for, not just what she is doing.
quests.explanation: Lonely is the feeling of wanting company or connection. Boredom is wanting something to do, while Mia is wishing for someone.
quests.funFact: Calling or messaging someone you like is a quick way to feel more connected.

quests.instruction: Everyone is praising Karan's cousin for her cricket trophy. Karan smiles, but inside he thinks, 'Why does everyone talk about her and not me?' Which word fits him?
quests.hint: He wants something that someone else is getting.
quests.explanation: Jealous is the feeling of wanting what someone else has, like attention or praise. The feeling is normal; what we do about it is what matters.
quests.funFact: Jealousy can be a clue about what you want. Asking 'What do I wish I had more of?' can help.

quests.instruction: During a power cut, a neighbor Hana barely knows brings candles to her family's door and offers to check on them later. How might Hana feel?
quests.hint: Think about how it feels when someone helps you without being asked.
quests.explanation: Grateful is the warm feeling we have when someone does something kind for us. It points to what they gave: care and help.
quests.funFact: Saying thank you is a way to share your gratitude with the person who helped.

quests.instruction: At recess, three classmates huddle over a game. When Dev walks up, they turn their backs and carry on without him. What is Dev likely feeling?
quests.hint: Was he invited into the group or kept apart?
quests.explanation: Left out is the feeling of being kept apart from a group when we want to be part of it. It is different from being alone by choice.
quests.funFact: Inviting someone to join takes just a sentence and can change their day.

quests.instruction: Anika has spent an hour on a poster, but her group changes the plan again, and she has to start over. Pick the word that fits best.
quests.hint: Think about effort that keeps getting wasted.
quests.explanation: Frustrated is what we feel when our effort keeps running into obstacles. The group is not attacking Anika, but the repeated changes are blocking her work.
quests.funFact: Agreeing on a plan before starting helps teams avoid redoing work.

quests.instruction: Lucy waves enthusiastically at a friend across the street, then realizes it is a stranger who waves back, puzzled. Her face turns hot. How might she feel?
quests.hint: Think about the moment she realizes the mix-up.
quests.explanation: A mix-up that others might notice can cause a hot face and an embarrassed feeling. It is normal and often funny later.
quests.funFact: Many people feel their face turn red when embarrassed because blood flows to the skin.

quests.instruction: Mr. Iyer reads aloud the story Kiran wrote and says it has the best details he has read this year. Kiran sits up straight, trying not to smile too widely. What is he feeling?
quests.hint: Notice that the praise is linked to something he made.
quests.explanation: Praise for work we put effort into brings pride. The straight posture and the hidden smile are clues.
quests.funFact: Being proud of your work does not mean you think you are better than others.

quests.instruction: Zoe wanted to be class messenger, but the teacher chooses someone else. Zoe nods quietly and sits down. What is the best word for it?
quests.hint: She hoped for something and it did not happen.
quests.explanation: Disappointed fits when we hoped for something and did not get it. Her quiet nod shows she is accepting it, but the feeling is still there.
quests.funFact: Telling the teacher you are interested in the next opportunity can turn a let-down into a plan.

quests.instruction: Since moving to a new town, Ahmed eats lunch beside people but does not know anyone yet. He misses having someone who gets his jokes. How might he feel?
quests.hint: Is anyone keeping him out, or does he simply lack close company so far?
quests.explanation: Nobody is excluding him, but he lacks close connection, so lonely fits better than left out. Left out is when a group keeps us out.
quests.funFact: Joining one club or activity can lead to finding your people more quickly.

quests.instruction: Pia's best friend has spent all week making plans with a new classmate, and Pia feels a pinch each time they laugh together. What might she be feeling?
quests.hint: Think about wanting something that someone else is getting.
quests.explanation: Jealous is the feeling of worrying we might lose someone's attention to another person. A pinch when they laugh together is a clue.
quests.funFact: Telling a friend, 'I miss spending time with you,' can help more than keeping the feeling inside.

quests.instruction: Sofia hears everyone talk about a weekend picnic she was not told about. Her stomach sinks as they plan the next one. How might she feel?
quests.hint: Think about being left off a plan that includes everyone else.
quests.explanation: Hearing about plans we were not part of can bring a sinking, left-out feeling. We wanted to belong and did not get the chance.
quests.funFact: Asking 'Can I join next time?' is a brave way to find out whether it was an accident.

quests.instruction: Mr. Patel stays after school to explain fractions again to Lena until she understands. She says, 'I could not have done it without your help.' What is she feeling?
quests.hint: Her words are a clue about how she sees his effort.
quests.explanation: When someone gives time and effort to help us, we can feel grateful. Her words show she values it.
quests.funFact: Saying exactly what someone did, like 'You stayed after school,' makes a thank-you more meaningful.

quests.instruction: During silent reading, Arjun's stomach growls loudly and a classmate giggles. He hides behind his book. Choose the best word.
quests.hint: Think about the moment he hid behind the book.
quests.explanation: A harmless body sound that others notice can cause embarrassment, even though it is completely normal.
quests.funFact: Everybody's stomach growls sometimes. It is just a sign of the body at work.

quests.instruction: Tia saves her pocket money for months and finally buys a gift for her grandmother all by herself. Walking home with the bag, she feels herself standing taller. What is the best word for it?
quests.hint: Think about what she did on her own and how long it took.
quests.explanation: A goal reached by ourselves after a long effort brings pride. The taller posture is a body clue.
quests.funFact: Saving up for something is a skill that grown-ups use all their lives.

quests.instruction: Everyone in the group agrees except Omar. When he tries to explain his idea for the third time, they say there is no time to listen. How might he feel?
quests.hint: He tries more than once and still is not heard.
quests.explanation: Being unable to get our idea across after several tries is frustrating. The group is not necessarily mean, but his effort keeps running into a wall.
quests.funFact: Writing an idea on paper and passing it around can help a quiet voice be heard.

quests.instruction: At a family wedding with lots of chatter, Hiro knows nobody his age and stands near the snack table, feeling distant from everyone. Choose the best word.
quests.hint: He is surrounded by people but not connected to anyone.
quests.explanation: A person can feel lonely even in a crowd when they do not have a connection with anyone. That is different from simply being alone.
quests.funFact: Being alone and feeling lonely are not the same. Some people enjoy being alone.

quests.instruction: Neha lies in bed, listening to her older sister stay up late laughing with cousins through the wall. She thinks, 'I want that too.' What might she feel?
quests.hint: Notice what she is wishing for that someone else has.
quests.explanation: Wanting what someone else gets, like staying up late with others, is jealousy. Noticing it is the first step in deciding what to do.
quests.funFact: Jealous feelings can fade when you find something to look forward to for yourself.

quests.instruction: Esha wanted to be on the team that goes to the district quiz, but the list is posted and she is the first reserve. How might she feel?
quests.hint: She hoped for one result and got a different one.
quests.explanation: She expected or hoped to be picked and was not, so disappointed fits. Being a reserve may help her feel hopeful, but the first feeling is the let-down.
quests.funFact: Being a reserve means you are ready to join if someone cannot play.

quests.instruction: When the cousins pick partners for the three-legged race, everyone pairs up and Jo is the one left at the edge. What is Jo likely feeling?
quests.hint: Think about being the only one without a partner.
quests.explanation: Being the only one without a partner can create a left-out feeling because he wanted to be part of the game.
quests.funFact: Teams can make an extra group so nobody is left over.

quests.instruction: On a rainy day, a stranger at the bus stop lifts her umbrella to cover Meera, who forgot hers. 'Thank you so much,' Meera says warmly. Which word describes this best?
quests.hint: Look at what the stranger did and how Meera responds.
quests.explanation: A kind act from someone we do not know can bring gratitude. Her warm thank-you shows it.
quests.funFact: Small acts of kindness can make a stranger's day better.

quests.instruction: Tuck's shirt has been on backward all day. He only notices at lunch when a friend points it out. How might he feel?
quests.hint: Think about discovering a mistake that others may have seen.
quests.explanation: Finding out we have been walking around with a silly mistake can make us feel embarrassed. Most people forget such moments quickly.
quests.funFact: Many people forget little mistakes like this quickly because they are busy with their own day.

quests.instruction: Rina's team picks up all the litter on the beach path. When the mayor thanks them, Rina looks at the clean sand and feels she did something good. Find the word that matches.
quests.hint: Think about the result they created together.
quests.explanation: Seeing the results of our own contribution, and being thanked for it, brings pride.
quests.funFact: Working together on a shared goal can make everyone feel proud.

quests.instruction: At the end of the school day, everyone leaves with someone. Josh packs his bag slowly, hoping someone will say, 'Walk with me?' How might he feel?
quests.hint: He is waiting for a connection that has not come.
quests.explanation: Hoping someone will invite us and watching others leave in pairs is a clear picture of loneliness.
quests.funFact: Starting a small chat, like 'Which way do you walk?', can begin a friendship.

quests.instruction: Ayaan's baby brother gets hugs and applause for his first steps. Ayaan peeks from behind the door with a twist in his tummy. What might he feel?
quests.hint: Think about who is getting all the attention.
quests.explanation: Wanting attention that a new baby is receiving is a very common type of jealousy. The twist in his tummy is a body clue.
quests.funFact: Older siblings often need extra time with grown-ups when a baby arrives.

quests.instruction: At the birthday dinner, the others laugh at an inside joke from a trip Dani did not join. She forces a smile but cannot follow the story. What is she feeling?
quests.hint: She is in the room, but not part of the shared story.
quests.explanation: Not sharing the experience that others are laughing about can make someone feel left out even when invited to the table.
quests.funFact: Asking, 'Can you tell me what happened?' invites someone back into a shared story.

quests.instruction: Samir explains where everyone should stand, but the team keeps going to the wrong spots and the match is slipping away. How might he feel?
quests.hint: He is trying to help, and it is not working yet.
quests.explanation: Giving clear directions that are not followed can feel frustrating, especially when something is on the line.
quests.funFact: Using a simple picture or drawing can help teammates understand where to go.

quests.instruction: Ria's cousin said she would come to her recital. The seat stays empty all through the performance. Choose the best word.
quests.hint: Think about what Ria was hoping for.
quests.explanation: She hoped someone she cares about would be there. When that did not happen, disappointed fits.
quests.funFact: Telling someone how their absence felt can lead to an apology and a plan for next time.

quests.instruction: When Pavan's bike chain snaps, three classmates take turns carrying his bag to school. 'Thank you, that meant a lot,' he says. What does he feel?
quests.hint: Look at his words and what his classmates did.
quests.explanation: Thank-you words after others went out of their way show gratitude. Helping each other builds trust.
quests.funFact: Gratitude is a feeling that tends to make people kinder to each other.
